about: Brittany Stevens, a Partner at Phillips & Associates | Sexual Harassment, Discrimination & Employment Lawyers, is a dedicated advocate for employees who have experienced sexual harassment, discrimination, and retaliation in the workplace. With a focus on employee-side representation, Brittany understands the unique challenges employees face and provides compassionate, empathetic counsel while fighting aggressively for their rights. Brittany’s client-first approach ensures that each person receives the support and legal expertise required to achieve the best possible outcomes in the most difficult circumstances. With a deep passion for justice and an unwavering commitment to her clients, Brittany works tirelessly to hold employers accountable and secure the compensation and protection that employees deserve.

Brittany has a proven track record of success in both federal and state courts, regularly handling claims under Title VII, the New York State Human Rights Law, and the New York City Human Rights Law. She also has extensive experience resolving matters prior to litigation, skillfully representing clients in mediations and other alternative dispute resolution forums to secure favorable outcomes. Brittany has recovered more than $40,000,000 in settlements for her clients.

Brittany has built a reputation for successfully representing individuals in complex disputes against high-powered C-suite executives and major corporations. She understands the power dynamics at play in these situations, as well as the inner workings and strategic defenses of large, well-resourced companies. This insight allows Brittany to navigate high-stakes negotiations and litigation with a precise, strategic approach, ensuring her clients' voices are heard and their rights protected, even when facing some of the most influential figures in the corporate world.

Brittany earned her undergraduate degree in Business Management from Skidmore College and her J.D. from the University of San Francisco School of Law. During law school, she interned with the Honorable Arthur Engoron in the New York Supreme Court, where she gained foundational experience in motion and trial practice.
